title: Temporary privileged-access escrow and on-call break-glass flow
creator: Aisha Kumar
project: Security: RBAC v2 and Admin Controls
description: Implement a controlled, auditable break-glass mechanism for emergency admin access that integrates with RBAC v2, SSO/SAML identity flows, and centralized audit logging. The feature will provide: 1) a temporary privilege escrow system (time-limited, scoped elevation), 2) an on-call activation flow with approval handoff and mandatory justification, and 3) end-to-end telemetry to detect misuse and enable post-incident review. This ticket covers design, prototype, and an initial rollout for on-call SREs and Security Engineers. Non-goals: UI polish for the Console and full enterprise policy editor - those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Security and IR leads
Break-glass activation requires either two-step on-call confirmation or SSO assertion + short-lived token issuance
All elevation events are recorded to audit-log pipeline with actor, justification, scope, TTL, and reason
Temporary credentials auto-revoke after TTL and on explicit action; revocation is observable in audit logs
RBAC v2 enforcement respects escrowed scopes (no privilege creep)
Simulated playbook executed in staging with no unauthorized access and audit trail validated
Basic telemetry/alerting for suspicious patterns (multiple activations by same user, long durations)
Operational runbook for post-incident debrief and rotation of credentials exists and is linked
tasks: Draft design spec: privilege escrow data model, tokens, and RBAC integration
Prototype escrow service that issues short-lived service tokens with scope tags
Integrate with SSO/SAML to support assertion-bound activation and MFA checks
Extend audit pipeline to ingest break-glass events with structured fields
Add CLI endpoint for on-call activation and Console API endpoint (internal-only)
Create staging playbook and run tabletop exercise with SRE/SEC/PM
Implement auto-revoke and emergency revocation hooks into token service
Create monitoring rules and PagerDuty runbook for suspicious activations
decisions: Use time-limited tokens (TTL) rather than mutable role toggles to reduce privilege persistence risk
Require justification text and attach to audit event; justify length limited to 512 chars
Two activation paths: 'on-call physical confirmation' (two on-call engineers) OR 'SSO assertion + security approver' depending on severity
Do not allow break-glass to expand scope beyond existing RBAC role unions; escrow only grants a subset of admin capabilities
Initial rollout limited to SRE security rotation and Security Engineers to minimize blast radius
Telemetry will be routed to security SIEM (Splunk) for correlation rather than ad-hoc Console tables

notes: Prototype uses a separate 'escrow' service to simplify audit capture and make revocations atomic
We deliberately avoid exposing a generic 'superuser' toggle to prevent long-lived high-privilege sessions
